text:
Maya P: Quick status — onboarding Tide13b (community fork). Smoke tests show weird token splits around ZWJ/ZWNJ and a downstream rotary phase drift after int4 conversion.
Raj K: Can you share the exact tokenizer example that fails?
Maya P: Yep. Small repro: `
input = 'Dr.\u200dKhan met at the mu\u200cseum'
# tokenized: ['Dr', '.', '\u200d', 'Khan', ' met', ' at', ' the', ' mu', '\u200c', 'seum']
`
Maya P: Tide's vocab contains explicit entries for U+200C and U+200D which splits sequences in a way we don't normally see with the llama/mistral family.
Oli (runtime): That can change token ids mid-context and break the assumptions used to build the rotary phase tables. Do we build rotary per-token-id or per-subword index during conversion?
Raj K: Tide's exporter kept rotary tied to token id ordering. Our llm_convert pipeline assumed control chars were normalized away and used index positions for mapping. Converter didn't apply NFKC normalization, so mapping slipped.
Sam QA: In the long context summarization runs we saw factuality regressions and some hallucination increases — not huge BLEU/Rouge shifts but noticeable on long prompts. Sounds like kv-cache misalign.
Maya P: Repro script:```python
from tide_tokenizer import Tokenizer
from tide_model import load_model

t = Tokenizer('tide_vocab.json')
print(t.encode('hello\u200cthere'))
```Output: `[6120, 3, 1741]` where `3` is the isolated ZWNJ id.
Raj K: The converter maps by array offsets in several places. If the source vocab has explicit control-char tokens not present in our reference, everything downstream shifts.
Oli (runtime): Rotary cache reads by position in kv cache; if the embedding for a token id is now a different logical subword the sin/cos phases are wrong — leading to subtle phase misalignments especially after quant.
Maya P: I tried a quick mitigation: wrap the tokenizer to normalize unicode to NFKC before encoding. That collapses the separated control char token and aligns ids with our expected mapping. Local smoke: rotary-looking errors reduced.
Raj K: Canonicalizing could change semantics for languages that rely on ZWJ/ZWNJ (Indic ligatures). We shouldn't unilaterally normalize without checking language coverage.
Sam QA: Metric diffs?
Maya P: Small 100-sample run: longctx QA EM 0.72 baseline, 0.68 after int4 conversion without fixes, with tokenizer NFKC wrapper up to 0.70. Partial improvement.
Oli (runtime): Another path: update the converter to explicitly detect U+200C/U+200D tokens and create an explicit mapping table. If target vocab lacks them, we can map them to nearest subtokens or optionally insert them and shift ids (ugly but deterministic).
Raj K: Also found a rotary metadata flag in Tide config: `rotary_scale: "1.02"`. That's a nontrivial multiplier. If our runtime assumes scale==1, small frequency mismatch gets amplified by int4 quantization noise.
Maya P: Right — quantization truncation + frequency mismatch => phase drift visible during generation.
Sam QA: Can runtime apply a compatibility shim for rotary_scale?
Oli (runtime): Yes — runtime has per-head rotary scaling support. I tested rescaling cached sin/cos by 1/1.02 at load time and re-ran an int4 smoke; hallucinations went down ~20%.
Raj K: Action items: 1) discuss tokenizer normalization policy (language safe approach). 2) improve converter to detect and remap control-char tokens explicitly. 3) make onboarding pipeline honor rotary_scale metadata (runtime shim). 4) add eval prompts covering ZWJ/ZWNJ named-entity cases.
Maya P: I'll file an RFC for tokenizer wrapper and follow-up PRs for conversion unit tests.
Oli (runtime): I'll add a runtime toggle to read rotary_scale from model metadata and rescale sin/cos on load. Default kept off until conversion flags compatibility.
onboard-bot: Checklist updated with `rotary_scale_detected` and `control_char_token_audit`.
Sam QA: Adding Indic name prompt-set to regression harness so future models don't slip.
Raj K: Also recommend an int8 calibration pass before forcing int4 — it helps capture scale offsets that int4 otherwise amplifies.
Maya P: Agree. Will run int8->int4 calibration and post calibration logs here.
Oli (runtime): Thanks. If rotary_scale is consistently present we can make deterministic rescale part of our loader to avoid touching tokenization.
Maya P: TL;DR: root cause appears to be combined: explicit ZWJ/ZWNJ tokens in Tide vocab + converter assumed normalization -> id offsets; plus rotary_scale mismatch -> quant amplifies phase drift. Plan: conservative converter remap + runtime rotary shim + expanded evals.
Raj K: Sounds good. :thumbsup:
Sam QA: Filing regression ticket now.
Maya P: Filing PRs and tickets, will link back when done.
